title: Teaching: surgical cricothyroidotomy
stem: Teaching room. A new junior doctor starts in your ED next week. Teach them how to perform an emergency surgical cricothyroidotomy on the part-task trainer, and briefly mention other techniques.

phases.title: Set the scene
phases.goal: Objectives and what they know already.

phases.title: Teach
phases.goal: Peyton's four steps, showing the DAS technique.

phases.title: Close
phases.goal: Feedback, and check what they will remember.

review.text: Technique. Your notes teach a number 11 blade, a tracheal hook, a Trousseau dilator and a 4–6 mm tube. The DAS emergency method is scalpel–bougie–tube: a size 10 blade, a bougie and a cuffed 6.0 tube. DAS 2025 makes a vertical midline skin incision with finger dissection the default in every adult, then a transverse stab through the membrane.

Age cut-off in children. Your notes' 12 years matches ATLS. The APA/DAS paediatric guideline uses a needle (cannula) technique from 1 to 8 years, allows a scalpel technique above about 8 years, and calls ENT for a tracheostomy under 1 year. Safe exam answer: needle under 12, surgical from 12, with 8–12 as the grey zone.

notes:
Checked against the Difficult Airway Society 2025 guideline (front-of-neck access) and the Peyton four-step approach to skills teaching.

Content: indication is can't intubate, can't oxygenate (CICO). DAS scalpel–bougie–tube: a size 10 scalpel, a bougie with a coudé tip, and a lubricated cuffed 6.0 tube. DAS 2025 makes a vertical midline skin incision (up to 8 cm, bottom to top) and finger blunt dissection to the membrane the default in every adult, then a transverse stab through the membrane with the cutting edge toward you, rotate the blade 90° so the sharp edge points to the feet, pull the blade toward you, slide the bougie along it, railroad the tube, inflate the cuff, confirm with capnography.

Your notes teach the older standard technique: a number 11 blade, a tracheal hook and a Trousseau dilator, and a 4–6 mm tube or tracheostomy tube. That is a recognised open technique but not the DAS emergency method; the station scores DAS and accepts the older method as 'other techniques'.

Blade: DAS specifies a size 10 (broad, curved) blade. Its width makes one stab wide enough for the bougie and a 6.0 tube, and the blade guides the bougie in. A size 11 (narrow, pointed) blade is not the DAS kit: the hole is often too small and needs extending, and the point more easily injures the back wall of the trachea. In the exam, say size 10. In real life, if only an 11 is available, still do the procedure, but widen the incision before passing the bougie.

Children (cut-offs differ by guideline): ATLS 10th says do not do a surgical cricothyroidotomy under 12 years; use needle cricothyroidotomy. The APA/DAS paediatric CICO guideline (children 1–8 years) uses cannula (needle) cricothyroidotomy, then an ENT scalpel or tracheostomy approach if that fails; over 8 years the membrane is usually big enough for a scalpel technique. Under 1 year, needle access is very difficult, so call ENT early for a tracheostomy. Your notes' 12 years matches ATLS. Safe exam answer: under 12, needle; 12 and over, surgical, with the 8–12 range as the grey zone where APA allows a scalpel technique. Complications and the SHORT mnemonic in your notes are correct.

Teaching method: set objectives, assess prior knowledge, then Peyton's four steps (demonstrate silently at real speed; demonstrate with explanation; learner talks you through; learner performs), feedback, check understanding, summary and plan.

Perfect script checked against DAS 2025 FONA, a Peyton teaching checklist, an HKCEM-style scheme and a keyword scheme. Removed the lecture-first and high-incision options and the unhelpful teaching replies.

steps.label: Talk to Dr Wan
steps.hint: Introduce, agree objectives, find out what they know.

turns.line: Hi, I'm Dr Wan. I've been told to learn the surgical airway?

opts.t: Hi, I'm the ED registrar. In ten minutes, you'll be able to do a scalpel–bougie–tube on the trainer. Sound OK?
opts.mark: Introduces self and sets a clear learning objective

opts.t: What do you know already: when would you do one?
opts.r: When you can't intubate and can't oxygenate?

opts.t: Demonstrate the whole procedure at real speed without talking
opts.mark: Peyton step 1: silent demonstration at real speed

opts.t: Repeat it slowly, explaining each step
Dr Wan talks you through it while you do it
opts.mark: Peyton step 3: learner narrates, you perform

opts.t: Dr Wan performs it, talking through each step
Kit: size 10 scalpel, bougie, lubricated cuffed 6.0 tube; neck extended; stand on the patient's left if right-handed
Laryngeal handshake: identify thyroid cartilage, membrane, cricoid
Vertical midline skin incision, bottom to top; blunt finger dissection to the membrane
opts.mark: Vertical midline incision and finger dissection (DAS 2025)

opts.t: Transverse stab through the membrane, cutting edge toward you
Rotate the blade 90° so the sharp edge points to the feet; pull it toward you
opts.mark: Rotates the blade and opens the hole

opts.t: Slide the bougie along the blade 10–15 cm into the trachea; remove the blade
Railroad the tube, inflate the cuff, confirm with capnography, secure

steps.label: Feedback and close
steps.hint: Ask how it went, give specific feedback, check understanding, summarise, plan.

opts.t: How do you think it went?
Your landmarks were excellent. Next time keep the blade in until the bougie is past it — it holds the hole open.
Tell me the three things you'll remember. Other methods: needle cricothyroidotomy in children, and the older hook-and-dilator technique. Practise on the trainer every week.
opts.r: Handshake, vertical cut, blade stays until the bougie's in.
opts.mark: Checks understanding, mentions other techniques, and agrees a plan

wrong: Transverse over a palpable membrane only
Collar incision above the sternal notch

qs.q: Which is part of the SHORT mnemonic for difficult front-of-neck access?

wrong: Yes, same technique with a 6.0 tube
Yes, with a larger vertical incision
Only if a tracheal hook is available
qs.why: ATLS: no surgical cricothyroidotomy under 12 years. APA: needle for ages 1–8, a scalpel technique possible over 8. Under 1 year: ENT tracheostomy.

badge.name: Teacher: FONA
badge.flavor: Handshake, vertical cut, stab, turn, bougie, tube.

cards.q: DAS scalpel–bougie–tube kit uses which blade?
cards.why: A broad size 10 blade makes a hole wide enough for a 6.0 tube in one stab and guides the bougie. A narrow 11 often needs the incision extended.
cards.note: Older notes: size 11 with hook and dilator.

cards.q: Tube size in the DAS front-of-neck technique?
cards.why: A 6.0 passes through the membrane opening over the bougie.

cards.q: After the transverse stab, the blade is rotated so the sharp edge faces…
options: Straight up, away from the neck
cards.why: Then pull it toward you to open the hole for the bougie.

cards.q: Which vessels lie near the upper cricothyroid membrane?
cards.why: Stay in the lower third of the membrane.

options: The learner talks the teacher through the procedure
The learner performs alone without comment
The teacher demonstrates silently at normal speed
The teacher breaks the skill into steps
cards.why: Step 3 forces active recall before the learner performs.

cards.q: Best first feedback question after a learner's attempt?
options: How do you think it went?

script.say: Hi, I'm the ED registrar. In ten minutes, you'll be able to do a scalpel–bougie–tube on the trainer: that's our learning objective. What do you know already: when would you do one?
Right: can't intubate, can't oxygenate. I'll teach it in Peyton's four steps. First, a silent demonstration at real speed.
Now slowly. Kit: a size 10 scalpel, a bougie, and a lubricated cuffed 6.0 tube; neck extended; I stand on the patient's left. Laryngeal handshake: thyroid cartilage, the membrane, the cricoid.

A vertical midline incision, bottom to top; finger dissection down to the membrane. A transverse stab through the membrane, cutting edge toward me. Rotate the blade 90 degrees so the sharp edge points to the feet, and pull it toward me.
Slide the bougie along the blade 10 to 15 cm into the trachea; blade out. Railroad the tube, inflate the cuff, confirm with capnography, secure it.
Step three: you talk me through it while I do it. Step four: you do it, talking through each step.
How do you think it went?
Your landmarks were excellent. Next time keep the blade in until the bougie is past it: it holds the hole open.
Tell me the three things you'll remember. Other methods: needle cricothyroidotomy in children, and the older hook-and-dilator technique. Practise on the trainer every week.
